issues.title: Make testing-methodology.md the repo's normative gate
issues.body:
CONTRIBUTING.md that points at docs/testing-methodology.md as normative, and a PR template asking which tiers were touched, which skipped, and why. The non-negotiables (never weaken a check; every fix ships its test; prove pre-existing by stashing) stated once, here.

**Acceptance.** Tests added with the change; each new assertion mutation-checked and the kill recorded in the PR; methodology tiers touched and skipped named in the PR.

issues.title: Cross-implementation vector format, and the first ten
issues.body:
tests/vectors/: a model, a question, the expected value, tolerance, and the `$fn` it holds at. Both sides compute it — our checks and the pinned provider — and neither is the oracle. First ten: volume, bbox, components, watertight, and interference/clearance on fixture parts. A vector only one side can compute is a finding about the other.

issues.title: Mutation-check convention and the CI step that enforces it
issues.body:
tools/mutate.sh: apply a named mutation, run the suite, assert the targeted test FAILS, restore. A CI step refuses a PR that adds tests without a recorded kill (a `MUTATION:` line in the commit or a file under tests/mutations/). The methodology's rule, mechanized.

**Acceptance.** Tests added with the change; each new assertion mutation-checked and the kill recorded in the PR; methodology tiers touched and skipped named in the PR.

issues.title: Envelope every provider answer: status, provenance, subject
issues.body:
Spec §07. Derive `ok|empty|refused|failed` from the provider's `empty`, `UNRESOLVED`, `valid` and diagnostics; attach model and params hashes and the kernel version; attach `subject.bbox`. **A verdict whose subject has zero extent is `refused`, never `ok`** — the overhang scan reported PASS on a part 80 mm away (mcp note 30).

**Acceptance.** Tests added with the change; each new assertion mutation-checked and the kill recorded in the PR; methodology tiers touched and skipped named in the PR.

issues.title: Known-positive controls beside every probe
issues.body:
Each interference/overhang/section probe runs a control geometry that MUST bite (a deliberate 48 mm² ledge; a deliberate overlap) and reports `controls.{ran,bit}`. A probe whose control did not bite is reported as such, not as clear. Caught a mutation driver that applied nothing and reported green.

**Acceptance.** Tests added with the change; each new assertion mutation-checked and the kill recorded in the PR; methodology tiers touched and skipped named in the PR.

issues.title: Pin view state at every measurement entry point
issues.body:
A parameter that moves geometry for display (`explode`) is a live input to every measurement through that file and does not look like one; the scan looked at empty space because of it (mcp note 30). Detect such parameters (Customizer group, name, or caller declaration) and pin them to zero in measurement calls, reporting that it did.

**Acceptance.** Tests added with the change; each new assertion mutation-checked and the kill recorded in the PR; methodology tiers touched and skipped named in the PR.

issues.title: `failed` never returns a path: audit every artifact-producing path
issues.body:
Every stale-artifact failure began with a tool that errored and left a previous good file in place (mcp notes 18, 26). Test: for every tool that can write a file, a forced failure produces no path in the result and leaves no file where the next call could read it.

**Acceptance.** Tests added with the change; each new assertion mutation-checked and the kill recorded in the PR; methodology tiers touched and skipped named in the PR.

issues.title: Async jobs: job.start / job.status, nothing blocks
issues.body:
Any call that can exceed a few seconds returns a job handle; `job.status` reports running|done|failed with progress. The provider has a 30–3600 s timeout and then a TIMEOUT error; a full overhang scan on the harness took 76 s. A timed-out MCP call is a lost turn and a tempting retry.

**Acceptance.** Tests added with the change; each new assertion mutation-checked and the kill recorded in the PR; methodology tiers touched and skipped named in the PR.

issues.title: Our own tool-surface budget test
issues.body:
Adopt the provider's idea: a test measuring the serialized JSON schema of every registered tool, failing past a total and a per-tool cap. Schema is paid on every request and tool-selection accuracy degrades as it grows. Caps to be set when the first real tools land; the test exists first.

issues.title: wm-process: support — the slicer criterion, not face normals
issues.body:
unsupported(z) = slice(z) MINUS offset(slice(z−h), +d), d = layer_h/tan(θ), over provider sections. Port overhang-scan.scad and validate against its four hand-computed shapes (flat cantilever 198.5≈197; 45° cone 0; 60° cone 0; 30° cone 131.1≈132.8). Distinguish bridge / droop / island (buildability 61). The provider's printability is facet-normal based; this is the thing it does not do.

issues.title: wm-process: critical angle from layer height and width
issues.body:
θ_crit = atan(layer_h / (0.5·width)). 45° only because 0.2 mm at 0.4 mm makes the ratio 1; 0.1 mm layers hold 26.6°. Refuse to call a region self-supporting without a declared layer height (spec §08).

issues.title: Provenance typing, weakest-input propagation, and 'what would I measure'
issues.body:
measured | literature | assumed | derived on every input; a derived claim inherits the weakest; `assumed` is reported as assumed however many decimals. Answer 'what would I have to measure to trust this' by the largest sensitivity × uncertainty. E for PETG is a literature range 1700–2200 (spec §08).

issues.title: Refusals: the four the spec names
issues.body:
Refuse to rank orientations without loads; to call a region self-supporting without a layer height; to report a clearance adequate without a process tolerance; to report a commanded value as achieved. Each is a place an answer was given that was true only under unstated assumptions (spec §08).

issues.title: Phase-gate reviews by a second reviewer
issues.body: Per the methodology: implementation to one reviewer, phase-gate review to another, reading the phase's tests against the methodology and the mutation-check records rather than the implementer's summary. Define the gate for each milestone here.
